objective: Create an idempotent, data-only SQL seed for an initialized GLPI 11 database that restores normalized long-lived organizational and asset data without restoring schema, runtime configuration, credentials, tickets, projects, logs, or recovery-backup content.

in: Audit the clean GLPI database against fresh GLPI defaults
Normalized employee users and contact data
Department groups, memberships, and required profile assignments
Locations, categories, manufacturers, types, models, states, printers, peripherals, and ownership relationships
A documented data-only SQL seed under services-library/project/glpi/export
Fresh GLPI 11.0.9 import and second-run verification
out: Core/default configuration, notification definitions, cron configuration, sessions, caches, logs, or events
Tickets, projects, tasks, followups, solutions, or operational history
Destructive wiping of an active production database
External identity, email, OAuth, or inventory integrations

constraints: Import only after GLPI initializes its schema and defaults.
Use stable source identifiers and natural-key lookups, not current numeric IDs.
A second run must not increase record or relationship counts.
Do not insert password hashes; imported users remain local-disabled pending authoritative identity integration.
Do not expose personal row data in verification output.
Keep recovery dumps distinct from the portable seed.
Do not commit or push without authorization.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A dependency audit identifies retained tables, source keys, required defaults, and excluded internal/operational tables.
The SQL contains data manipulation only, performs no schema DDL, and excludes tickets, projects, runtime logs, configuration, and password hashes.
Import into freshly initialized GLPI 11.0.9 recreates expected normalized users, groups, memberships, profiles, locations, categories, references, printers, peripherals, and ownership relationships.
A second run creates no duplicates and preserves verified counts.
The seed is documented as a portable long-lived-data bootstrap rather than a recovery backup or destructive reset and passes review.

assessment.reason: A portable relational seed must map multiple GLPI entity families without fixed IDs, secrets, duplicates, or operational history.
surfaces: Users, groups, profiles, references, assets, and relationship tables
unknowns: Which reference rows are imported versus defaults without source markers.
Whether every user has a stable registration_number.
Which ownership/contact relationships require polymorphic links.

practices.practice: Compare retained rows with a fresh GLPI baseline and map dependencies.
practices.reason: The seed must exclude defaults and internal rows.

practices.practice: Generate deterministic SQL using source keys, natural-key lookups, and idempotent upserts.
Import into freshly initialized GLPI twice and verify counts and relationships.
practices.reason: Fresh-install and repeat-run behavior define portability.

practices.practice: Inspect the SQL contract and obtain independent review.
practices.reason: The artifact contains sensitive relational data.

obligations.text: Audit retained data families and fresh-default differences with stable mapping keys.
Generate the data-only idempotent SQL seed without schema, secrets, or operational history.
Import the seed into freshly initialized GLPI and verify retained data and relationships.
Run the seed a second time and prove counts do not increase.
Document intended use and review data-only boundaries and safety.

evidence.summary: Model self-review of the live-versus-fresh audit confirms fresh GLPI 11.0.9 contributes only five default users and four profile assignments across the retained families. All retained business families are absent from a fresh baseline. Imported users are uniquely resolvable by 56 registration numbers plus 18 unique login-name fallbacks; groups and references have unique root-scoped names; printers and peripherals have complete unique otherserial keys; all memberships, profile links, ownership, and asset reference relationships resolve without orphans. Tickets, projects, configuration, logs, events, cron data, and credentials are not dependencies of the portable set.

args:
set -euo pipefail; OUT=services-library/project/glpi/export/data-portable-seed.sql; sha256sum -c "$OUT.sha256"; test "$(stat -c %a "$OUT")" = 600; test "$(stat -c %a "$OUT.sha256")" = 600; python3 - <<'PY'
import re
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('services-library/project/glpi/export/data-portable-seed.sql')
s=p.read_text()
body=re.sub(r'^--.*$', '', s, flags=re.M)
statements=[x.strip() for x in body.split(';') if x.strip()]
assert not any(re.match(r'^(CREATE|DROP|ALTER|TRUNCATE|REPLACE|GRANT|LOCK|UNLOCK)\\b', x, re.I) for x in statements)
allowed={'glpi_manufacturers','glpi_printermodels','glpi_peripheraltypes','glpi_states','glpi_locations','glpi_itilcategories','glpi_groups','glpi_users','glpi_useremails','glpi_profiles_users','glpi_groups_users','glpi_printers','glpi_peripherals'}
inserts=re.findall(r'INSERT INTO `([^`]+)`',body)
updates=re.findall(r'UPDATE `([^`]+)`',body)
assert set(inserts)==allowed and set(updates)==allowed
assert len(inserts)==374 and len(updates)==374
for forbidden in ['glpi_tickets','glpi_projects','glpi_logs','glpi_events','glpi_crontasklogs','glpi_configs','glpi_sessions','glpi_queuednotifications','glpi_queuedwebhooks']:
    assert forbidden not in body
assert not re.search(r'`(?:password|password_history|personal_token|api_token|cookie_token|2fa|user_dn)`',body,re.I)
assert 'START TRANSACTION;' in s and 'COMMIT;' in s
assert 'Apply only after GLPI has initialized its own empty schema and defaults.' in s
assert not re.search(r'@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+',body)
print('portable-seed-static-verification=passed')
PY

evidence.summary: Model self-review of data-portable-seed.sql confirms it contains no schema DDL or destructive statements; writes only 13 curated long-lived business tables; references no tickets, projects, configuration, sessions, queues, logs, or events; contains no password, token, 2FA, or directory-auth columns; exposes no raw email literals; wraps changes in a transaction; and explicitly requires an initialized empty GLPI. Dependencies use root-scoped natural names, the existing Self-Service profile name, user registration/login keys, and unique asset otherserial keys rather than current numeric IDs. The validated fresh-import smoke test also confirmed zero imported password hashes.

decisions.text: Target an already initialized GLPI schema and include no schema DDL.
Create a clean slate by initializing fresh GLPI then applying the seed, not by deleting an active system.
Retain identity/contact data without reusable local password hashes.

risks.text: Fixed IDs could connect data to wrong defaults.
risks.mitigation: Resolve dependencies through source or natural keys.

risks.text: Upserts could mutate unrelated same-name records.
risks.mitigation: Prefer source identifiers and fail on ambiguity.

risks.text: The SQL contains personal and asset data.
risks.mitigation: Restrict permissions, avoid row output, checksum, and do not commit without authorization.
